text:
anna: FYI I just pushed the int4 quantized build of model-x into staging and noticed a reproducible divergence when prompts exceed ~9k tokens. The float16 baseline is fine.
jorge: Can you paste a minimal repro prompt + outputs?
anna: Yep. Repro steps in order:
1) checkout branch release/int4-modelx
2) run ./run_eval --model staging/model-x:int4 --prompt-file tests/long_prompts/anchored_story.txt --max-tokens 2048
3) compare output to staging/model-x:fp16
Here are the two outputs diff (trimmed):
```
-- fp16: "The caravan reached the valley at dawn, and the elders set the treaty aside to listen to the wind."
++ int4: "The caravan reached the valley at dawn, and the elders set the treaty aside to listen to the window."
```
The substitution "wind" -> "window" is indicative; it's not a single token off-by-one, it's semantic drift after long prefix.
mei: Hmm interesting. Do you see drift only after a specific anchor token or after a certain distance from the priming segment?
anna: It's distance-dependent. With a short 512 primer there's no drift. With primers >8192 tokens it slowly starts to diverge around token 9200.
sam: Could be RoPE scaling mismatch after quantization. Any rotary/pos-embed changes in the quant pipeline?
anna: We only changed weight dtype packing; we do apply dynamic scale folding in kv cache transform to reduce memory. No intentional pos-embed code changes. But I did notice the quant conversion script uses a slightly different rotary scaling factor (legacy fallback) for odd seq lengths.
jorge: Can you paste the snippet where you build the KV cache/rotary scaling?
anna: Sure:
```
# in kv_cache.py
def compute_rotary_scale(seq_len, base=10000):
    # legacy heuristic used in quant packer
    return (seq_len / base) ** 0.5
# used when packer=True
```
This diverges from the fp16 runtime where we use a linear clamp.
mei: That heuristic looks suspicious. On fp16 we use: scale = min(1.0, target_len / seq_len), whereas this sqrt-based scale will under/over scale at large seqs.
sam: Quick experiment: run the int4 binary but patch kv_cache.compute_rotary_scale to call the fp16 codepath (monkeypatch) and re-run one prompt. If it matches fp16 then we found it.
anna: I tried that locally — monkeypatching to the fp16 linear clamp removed the semantic drift entirely on the long prompt (outputs identical for first 2k tokens and same content semantics through 12k).
ci-bot: perf-test #4912 completed — int4-staging end-to-end latency 12% lower vs fp16.
jorge: Great find. So the quant packer inadvertently changed the rotary scale heuristic for large seqs. Two action items: 1) revert that heuristic in the packer; 2) run a full quant-compare eval set to ensure no other regressions (long-context fidelity bench).
anna: I'm opening a small PR that replaces the heuristic with the fp16 linear clamp and adds unit tests for seq_len = [256,1024,8192,16384]. PR: https://git.redwood/modelx/pull/234
mei: Also add a regression test that runs a couple of anchored-story prompts through the eval harness with seed fixed; we should fail the build if perplexity gap > 0.8 and edit distance > 2 after 10k tokens.
sam: For thoroughness run the quantized model with kv cache warmstart (prefill) and coldstart too; some errors only show up post-warmstart.
anna: Logged both test runs into CI: see artifacts in PR. Quick note — int4 performance numbers look good, but we must ensure we don't silently change RoPE semantics during packing.
jorge: Do we want a hotfix release for current customer test pools?
mei: Yes — flag as P0 for staging-only customers. If we don't ship int4 to prod until we run the full eval it's fine, but staging needs rollback/hotfix.
ci-bot: deploy rollback triggered for staging/model-x:int4 -> staging/model-x:fp16 by @mei
anna: Thanks. I'll follow up with a postmortem note and add the test vectors to the long-context bench.
sam: One more ask — can we add a small fuzz harness that randomizes seq_len and compares kv cache states between fp16 and int4 after prefill to catch edge scaling cases?
anna: Yep adding that to my PR as a python pytest (fuzzer seed) + a triage checklist.
jorge: Perfect. Great debugging chain, nice find. :tada:
mei: Nice work @anna.
